title: Machine-learning screening identifies two drug-repurposing candidates against tuberculosis
summary: A virtual-screening workflow combined XGBoost and graph-neural-network models to screen 11,576 DrugBank compounds. Researchers selected 15 candidates for evaluation; four met the study’s activity cutoff against Mycobacterium tuberculosis H37Rv. Aldoxorubicin and quarfloxin were further tested against multidrug-resistant isolates, intracellular bacteria and recombinant DNA gyrase. These are laboratory repurposing results, not evidence of patient benefit or clinical safety. A same-team patent-family publication predates the journal article; this record makes no priority claim over patent disclosures. Concentration values are omitted because of inconsistent units in the rendered tables.
ai_technology: Ensemble virtual screening with XGBoost and graph neural networks
organization: Institute for Artificial Intelligence & Department of Computer Science and Technology, Tsinghua University

evidence.tested: The article reports follow-up testing of 15 selected compounds, four meeting the authors’ activity cutoff against H37Rv, and additional assays of aldoxorubicin and quarfloxin against multidrug-resistant isolates and recombinant DNA gyrase.
evidence.unknown: All reported results are in vitro. The study does not establish patient efficacy, clinical safety or the compounds’ cellular mechanism. Precise concentration values are omitted because table units are inconsistent; an earlier patent-family publication is noted without a priority claim.
evidence.ai_role: Multiple learned models, including XGBoost and graph neural networks, predicted antitubercular activity in a DrugBank screen and contributed to selection of candidates for experimental evaluation.

source_review.scope: Primary Oxford Academic full indexed article, including abstract, Methods, results, article history and author affiliations; patent-family chronology checked from the patent family page. A-version patent text was not reviewed.
